第 82 章 Team Stability Matters团队稳定很重要

Bill Horvath / 比尔·霍瓦斯

— 第 225 页 —

If you're running an engineering department, you may find yourself tempted to move people around between teams to address fluctuations in demand from customers and other business stakeholders. While we welcome changing requirements, even late in development, changing team composition to address them is a mistake. Why? Teams that stay together are better, in all kinds of measurable ways. All else being equal, a team with stable membership will perform better over time. And there's lots of empirical data to back this up: studies show team stability leads to high performance, predictable velocity, and outcome quality, just to name a few.

如果你在运营一个工程部门，你可能发现自己忍不住在团队之间调动人来应对客户和其他业务利益相关者的需求波动。虽然我们欢迎变化的需求，即使在开发后期，改变团队构成来应对它们是错误的。为什么？在一起的团队更好，在各种可衡量的方面。其他条件相同，成员稳定的团队随时间表现更好。有很多实证数据支持这一点：研究显示团队稳定带来高绩效、可预测的 velocity、结果质量，仅举几例。

Team performance data only has meaning when the team membership doesn't change. Some software development teams measure their performance in terms of velocity; others use measures of code quality (such as bugs that escaped into production); still others use even simpler gauges, such as number of features delivered. But regardless of the data that's collected, the more the team's membership changes, the less meaningful the data becomes, because the unit of measurement has changed. A stable team's work metrics have meaning because the team is stable.

团队绩效数据只有在团队成员不变时才有意义。一些软件开发团队用 velocity 衡量绩效；其他用代码质量衡量（如逃到生产的 bug）；还有用更简单的指标，如交付的功能数。但不管收集什么数据，团队成员变化越多，数据越没意义，因为测量单位变了。稳定团队的工作指标有意义是因为团队稳定。

There's an interactive effect between team stability and product owner effectiveness. In an Agile shop, the product owner constructs work items with the capabilities and past performance of the team in mind. Their knowledge of the team can have a profound impact on how the product owner writes the work items, and where they place them in the backlog. As the product owner's knowledge of the team grows, their ability to write consistently sized work items that the team can easily estimate and execute becomes better and better. Their performance becomes stable, which means it's predictable.

团队稳定和产品负责人有效性之间有交互效应。在敏捷商店，产品负责人带着团队能力和过往绩效构造工作项。他们对团队的了解可以深刻影响产品负责人怎么写工作项、放在待办哪里。随着产品负责人对团队了解增长，他们写大小一致、团队容易估算和执行的工作项的能力越来越好。他们的绩效变得稳定，意味着可预测。

— 第 226 页 —

Predictable performance means it's easier to roadmap features, especially with a well-maintained backlog. If several sprints-worth of stories at the top of the backlog are sized, it's easy to see the impact that changing the order or adding new features will have on the product roadmap. Psychological safety is positively correlated with team effectiveness and negatively correlated with membership changes. Recent research shows a strong negative correlation between team tenure diversity (i.e., variability in how long the members have been on the team) and team psychological safety, which predicts team effectiveness. In other words, the more a team changes, the less likely it is that its members will trust one another, and the greater the odds that they'll lose effectiveness as a result.

可预测的绩效意味着更容易做功能路线图，尤其是有维护良好的待办时。如果待办顶部几个 sprint 的故事已经 sizing，很容易看到改变顺序或加新功能会对产品路线图有什么影响。心理安全和团队有效性正相关，和成员变化负相关。最近研究显示团队任期多样性（即成员在团队时间的变异性）和团队心理安全之间强负相关，心理安全预测团队有效性。换句话说，团队变化越多，成员越不可能互相信任，他们因此失去有效性的几率越大。

A Possible Solution to Pressure压力的可能解决方案

Depending on the discretion you're granted, you might not be able to directly resist stakeholder demands to move people between teams in order to meet deadlines. Aside from pointing out the one-month birth fallacy, there are other approaches that you might consider. For example, you might have a roaming "firefighter" team whose role is to acquire knowledge across products and supplement teams under pressure by pulling tickets from their backlog that are relatively independent of the rest of pressured-team's work. This kind of approach works particularly well when the department has well-documented definitions of done that include stringent quality-control measures such as automated testing and code reviews of every commit. Regardless of your chosen approach, you'll find it well worth your while to defend the stability of your development teams—their psychological safety (and perhaps yours) depends on it.

取决于你被授予的裁量权，你可能无法直接拒绝利益相关者为赶截止日期在团队间调人的要求。除了指出一个月生出来的谬误，还有其他方法你可以考虑。例如，你可以有一个流动的「消防员」团队，其角色是跨产品获取知识，通过从压力团队的待办中拉相对独立于其他工作的工单来补充他们。这种方法在部门有文档良好的完成定义、包含严格质量控制措施如自动测试和每次提交代码评审时特别有效。不管你选哪种方法，你会发现捍卫开发团队的稳定非常值得——他们的心理安全（也许还有你的）取决于此。
